title: lore sync destroys log.md entries it cannot re-derive: regeneration replaces instead of merging
description:
`lore sync` regenerates `docs/log.md` by WHOLE-FILE REPLACEMENT, so any entry it can no
longer re-derive from the visible git history is destroyed. Reported by the quest-cli
session on 2026-09-11 and routed here by opum-agent; the bundle format is ours, so the
fix is ours.

REPRODUCED FIRST-PARTY IN THIS REPO, 2026-09-11, not merely taken on the peer's word.
lore-cli's own history was rebuilt on 2026-09-10 (LCLI-468, single root commit e3d7586),
so its committed `docs/log.md` holds 324 entries for commits unreachable from HEAD. A
single `lore sync` — fired incidentally by the opum-workflow PostToolUse hook — rewrote
the file from 328 lines to 5: `1 insertion, 324 deletions`. Restored with `git checkout`
before anything was committed. This repository is therefore both the owner of the defect
and a live instance of it, and anyone running `lore sync` here will silently stage the
same wipe.

ORIGINAL REPORT (quest-cli): every `lore sync` rewrote its `docs/log.md` from 282 lines
to 4, deleting 279 dated entries, five times before it was noticed. That repo was deleted
and recreated on 2026-09-10 (OPAG-70). It has stopped regenerating log.md and reverts the
file on every sync until this is fixed.

VERIFIED IN CODE:
- `src/commands/sync.ts` `regenerateIndexAndLog()` builds `logBytes` from
  `buildLog(gitAdapter, {to: headSha}, {root: DOCS_DIR})` and, if the bytes differ at
  all, writes the WHOLE file: `writes.set(LOG_FILE, {before: existingLog, after:
  logBytes})`. The existing bytes are read only to compare, never to merge. Note the
  contrast three lines above in the same function: index regeneration already passes the
  on-disk bytes in as `generateIndexes(graph, {existing: diskIndexBytes})`, so an
  existing-aware regeneration seam is already precedent here.
- `src/core/log.ts` `generateLog()` is pure over the commit set it is handed. It is not
  buggy — it faithfully renders the history it can see. The loss happens at the write.
- The peer described it as a "managed block"; it is not. `log.md` has no managed-block
  markers, it is a whole generated file. The fix cannot lean on `core/managed-block.ts`
  and has to live in the log path.

WHY `lore check` STAYS GREEN ON THE TRUNCATED FILE: `core/log.ts`'s header documents an
explicit ADR-0007 drift-gate exemption — a git-derived log.md changes on every commit, so
it is materialized at sync time and EXCLUDED from check's regenerate-and-compare gate,
precisely so it does not report permanent drift or break on shallow CI checkouts. There
is no gate to teach; the exemption is deliberate and the loss is invisible by design.

WHY THIS BELONGS IN LORE, NOT IN A PER-REPO WORKAROUND: a history rewrite is only one way
to reach this state. A shallow clone (`--depth`), a grafted history, a CI checkout with
limited fetch depth, or a pruned range all present lore with a history that is a strict
subset of what the committed log records, and all produce the same silent truncation.
Every consumer running `lore sync` in CI is exposed, with no rewrite involved.

RULING THAT FRAMES IT (opum-agent, 2026-09-11): dated logs are history under the fleet
retirement-scope rule, and a regeneration that can only see post-rewrite commits is
lossy, not authoritative.

PROPOSED SHAPE (the peer's, and it fits the code): make log regeneration a MERGE rather
than a replace. Parse the committed `log.md` into entries, key them by commit hash, union
with the newly derived entries, re-render deterministically. The result is a superset:
entries whose commits are unreachable are preserved under their recorded folder section,
newly derivable entries are added. In the normal case (history only grows) merged output
is byte-identical to today's, so idempotency and byte-stability are unaffected.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR DESIGN, deliberately not decided here:
- Where the merge belongs. `generateLog` is contractually pure and order-independent; the
  cleanest seam is an `{existing}` option mirroring `generateIndexes`, keeping the merge
  pure and the parse total.
- A rewritten commit (same change, new hash) yields BOTH entries under superset
  semantics. That is the honest outcome for a log of history, but it should be a
  documented decision, not a side effect.
- Whether an unparseable or hand-edited committed log fails loudly or is preserved
  verbatim. Preserving is safer, failing is louder. Pick one and say why.
- Whether `lore sync` should report the log delta (added vs preserved) rather than just
  counting a changed file. Silence at the sync boundary is half of why quest-cli went
  five syncs without noticing.

NOT OURS, recorded only so nobody chases it: opum-workflow's PostToolUse hook fires
`lore sync` on a text match against the Bash command string rather than on a real tracker
write. Confirmed here — it fired after a `quest task create` that FAILED with a usage
error and never wrote anything, and that no-op is what staged the 324-line deletion
above. Routed to opum-fleet.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `lore sync` in a repository whose committed docs/log.md holds entries for commits unreachable from HEAD preserves those entries; the regenerated file is a superset, never smaller
Where the visible history is a superset of the committed log (the normal case), output is byte-identical to today's, so idempotency and byte-stability are unchanged
A shallow or depth-limited checkout is covered by the same path as a rewritten history, proven by a test, since it is the case a consumer hits in CI without any rewrite happening
The rewritten-commit case (old and new hash both present) is decided deliberately and documented in core/log.ts's header contract
The parse of an existing log.md is total: a hand-edited or malformed file has a defined, tested outcome rather than a crash or a silent wipe

The ADR-0007 drift-gate exemption for log.md is re-examined and either left in place with the reason restated, or narrowed; merge semantics may make shrinkage impossible by construction, which beats a warning
This repository's own docs/log.md survives a `lore sync` intact, since it is a live instance of the defect
`lore check` exits 0 and the full test suite passes

finalSummary:
Fixed in PR #6, CI run 34662560342 — all 12 checks green on that exact SHA (2 skipped promotion jobs), squash-landed to dev.

WHAT CHANGED: `lore sync` regenerated docs/log.md by whole-file replacement; it now merges. `generateLog` takes the committed bytes as `options.existing`, derived entries render from git history, and any committed entry the visible history cannot account for is carried forward under the folder it was recorded in. The result is a superset. `sync.ts` passes the committed bytes on BOTH paths — the no-HEAD branch needed it just as much, since an unresolvable HEAD is the emptiest possible history and replaced the whole file rather than truncating part of it.

PROVEN, not asserted:
- This repo, before: one `lore sync` staged `1 insertion, 324 deletions`. After: `1 insertion` — the single entry the rebuilt history does make derivable — with all 324 preserved, and a second sync reports `0 files changed`.
- 14 new tests. 9 of them were verified to FAIL against the previous behaviour by reverting src/ and re-running; the other 5 are no-regression guards that must pass either way. Full suite 2915 pass / 0 fail, tsc clean, `lore check` exit 0.
- The two pre-existing `log.md is a full-history projection` tests pass untouched, which is the byte-identical-in-the-normal-case claim holding rather than being taken on faith.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS IN THE DESCRIPTION, all now decided and documented in core/log.ts's header contract:
- The merge lives behind an `{existing}` option on the pure `generateLog`, mirroring the seam `generateIndexes` already used three lines away in the same function.
- A rewritten commit appears under BOTH hashes. Deliberate: the two are indistinguishable from two genuine commits, and a log that over-reports history is recoverable by reading it where one that under-reports is not.
- A malformed or hand-edited log preserves what is legible rather than failing. Failing the sync over a file lore itself generated would leave a repository unable to sync at all; preserving loses nothing.
- The merge keys on (timestamp, hash), not the whole entry line, so an entry written by an older lore whose subject rendered differently is recognised as the same commit instead of being carried forward as a duplicate. Derived entries are never de-duplicated against each other, so the existing contract that two commits sharing an abbreviated hash stay distinct still holds.
- Carried-forward subjects are emitted verbatim. Re-rendering would feed an already-escaped subject back through renderSubject and grow its code-span delimiter by one backtick per sync.

ADR-0007's drift-gate exemption is AMENDED, NOT NARROWED, and that is the part worth carrying forward. The exemption is a reason, not an oversight: a git-derived log changes on every commit, so gating it would report permanent drift and break on shallow CI checkouts. Merge semantics make a shrinking log.md impossible by construction, which is a stronger guarantee than a gate reporting the loss after the fact — so the exemption can stay and no longer hides anything. quest-cli, who reported this, had framed it as a missing check and agreed the construction fix was the better one.

WHAT REMAINS OUTSIDE THIS TASK, recorded so it is not mistaken for done: every fleet session runs the published npm binary, so this fix reaches nobody until @opum-ai/lore ships it. quest-cli's ruling to keep reverting its log.md stands until then, and 0.6.1 is being cut for that reason with the user's authorization. The last acceptance criterion below is checked against this repository's working tree and CI, not against any consumer's installed binary.

The sync-boundary question in the description — that "1 file(s) changed" is the wrong unit — was NOT fixed here. It is not lore's; opum-fleet took it as OFLE-31, and every rewritten file now carries its delta with an inspect-first notice when a file loses more than it gains.

Reported by quest-cli (279 entries lost across five syncs), routed by opum-agent, reproduced first-party here (324 entries) during triage.



ADDENDUM, same PR: a CRLF defect in the fix itself, found by inspection after the first green run and before the merge. JavaScript's `$` without the `m` flag matches at end of input or before a final `\n`, never before a `\r`, so on a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true NEITHER the heading nor the entry pattern matched a single line. parseEntries would have yielded nothing, the merge would have carried nothing forward, and regeneration would have degraded silently back to replace semantics -- on one platform, with every test green, because every fixture is written with \n. Fixed by stripping a trailing CR at parse time (not render time, so a carried-forward entry is byte-identical to a derived one), with two tests that fail without it. Worth recording as a class, not an incident: a text parser added to this codebase is not covered by its own tests unless one fixture uses the line ending the other platform actually produces.

Also recorded so it is not misread later: the windows-latest job failed once on the closure SHA, on `cli — init dispatch ... (LORE-260)` timing out at 60s. That test is unrelated to this change and passed on the identical code in the first run. It is a flake, not a signal, and it is not what surfaced the CRLF defect -- inspection did.
